story_type: movie crew returns from space, Soyuz landing
hook: They flew to space to shoot a movie. This is the landing.
narration: This capsule slammed into the steppe of Kazakhstan with an actress and a film director inside.
Twelve days earlier, Yulia Peresild and Klim Shipenko had flown to the space station to film scenes for a movie called Challenge.
Their ride home was cosmonaut Oleg Novitskiy, finishing one hundred ninety one days in orbit.
On October sixteenth, twenty twenty one, their Soyuz pulled away from the station.
A Soyuz comes down under one huge parachute, and small engines fire just above the ground to soften the hit.
[short pause] Recovery helicopters were already circling the dust cloud.
outcome: Recovery crews lifted all three out of the Soyuz on the steppe of Kazakhstan.
title: Movie crew lands back from space
description:
On Oct. 17, 2021, cosmonaut Oleg Novitskiy, actress Yulia Peresild and director Klim Shipenko landed in Kazakhstan in their Soyuz MS-18 after 12 days of filming a movie aboard the International Space Station.

facts.claim: Novitskiy, Peresild and Shipenko undocked Oct. 16 and landed in Kazakhstan Oct. 17
facts.source_quote: undocked from the International Space Station’s Nauka Multipurpose Laboratory Module in their Soyuz MS-18 spacecraft October 16, returning to Earth a few hours later for a parachute-assisted landing on the steppe of Kazakhstan Oct. 17

facts.claim: Actress and director spent 12 days filming a movie called Challenge
facts.source_quote: Peresild, a Russian actress and Shipenko, her producer-director, spent 12 days on the station filming scenes for a movie title “Challenge”
Novitskiy returned after spending 191 days in space
